# Preface {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the **AI Engineering Handbook** — a from-scratch, hands-on path
that takes you from *"I can write a little Python"* to *"I can build, train,
and ship intelligent systems."*

**Who this book is for.** It assumes no prior knowledge of machine learning.
Every concept is built up from first principles, with the mathematics
explained (and, where it helps, proved), concrete worked examples, and
runnable, heavily commented code.

**How each chapter is organized.** We follow the same rhythm throughout:
learning objectives → intuition → formalism and proofs → worked examples →
annotated code → exercises → references to the primary literature.

**How to read it.** Read the intuition first, then the formalism; do the
worked examples by hand; run and modify the code. The exercises are where the
understanding actually forms.

> This is a living draft. Chapters are released and refined incrementally.
